Step_Length.description: Step Length: Anterior-posterior distance between heel-strike of one leg, to heel-strike of the other leg. The left mean/std graph values were calculated for the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated for the right leg.

Stride_Length.description: Stride Length: Anterior-posterior distance between heel-strike to the following heelstrike of the same leg. The left mean/std graph values were calculated for the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated for the right leg.

Step_Width.description: Step Width: Medio-lateral distance between the leg at mid-stance, and the following step of the opposite leg at mid-stance

Stance_Time.description: Stance Time: Length of time the foot is in contact with the ground. Measured from heel-strike until toe-off for all steps in each leg. The left mean/std graph values were calculated for the left stance, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated for the right stance.

Swing_Time.description: Swing Time: Length of time the foot is in the air between steps. Measured from toe-off until heel-strike for all steps in each leg. The left mean/std graph values were calculated for the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated for the right leg.

Single_Support_Percent.description: Single Support: Percent of the stride when only one foot is in contact with the ground. The left mean/std graph values were calculated for the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated for the right leg.

Double_Support_Percent.description: Double Support: Percent of the stride when both feet are in contact with the ground. The left mean/std graph values were calculated for the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated for the right leg.

Lateral_Pelvis_Sway.description: Lateral pelvis sway: maximum medio-lateral distance travelled by the pelvis over one full stride. Ensure that the calibration board is placed perpendicular to the walking direction.

Mid_Swing_Ankle_Height_Diff.description: Mid-swing ankle height difference: distance between the swinging ankle and the stance ankle at mid-swing. This is a minimum foot clearance related measure.

Ankle_Heelstrike.description: Heelstrike: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the ankle at heelstrike. Postive values indicate dorsiflexion and negative values indicate plantar flexion. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Ankle_Mid_stance.description: Mid-stance: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the ankle at mid-stance (when the ankle is directly beneath the hip joint centre). Postive values indicate dorsiflexion and negative values indicate plantar flexion. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Ankle_Toeoff.description: Toeoff: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the ankle at toeoff. Postive values indicate dorsiflexion and negative values indicate plantar flexion. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Ankle_Mid_swing.description: Mid-swing: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the ankle at mid-swing (when the ankle is directly beneath the hip joint centre). Postive values indicate dorsiflexion and negative values indicate plantar flexion. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Ankle_Peak_dorsiflexion.description: Peak dorsiflexion of the ankle over the entire gait cycle. Postive values indicates dorsiflexion and negative values indicates plantar flexion. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Ankle_Peak_plantar_flexion.description: Peak plantar flexion of the ankle over the entire gait cycle. Postive values indicates dorsiflexion and negative values indicates plantar flexion. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Ankle_ROM.description: Range of Motion (ROM): Anterior-posterior ROM of the ankle joint over an entire gait cycle (heelstrike to heelstrike). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Knee_Heelstrike.description: Heelstrike: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the knee at heelstrike. Postive values indicates flexion. NOTE, the simulated knee is locked and can never be extended beyond 0 degress (straight leg). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Knee_Mid_stance.description: Mid-stance: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the knee at mid-stance (when the ankle is directly beneath the hip joint centre). Postive values indicates flexion. NOTE, the simulated knee is locked and can never be extended beyond 0 degress (straight leg). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Knee_Toeoff.description: Toeoff: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the knee at toeoff. Postive values indicates flexion. NOTE, the simulated knee is locked and can never be extended beyond 0 degress (straight leg). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Knee_Mid_swing.description: Mid-swing: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the knee at mid-swing (when the ankle is directly beneath the hip joint centre). Postive values indicates flexion. NOTE, the simulated knee is locked and can never be extended beyond 0 degress (straight leg). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Knee_Peak_flexion.description: Peak flexion of the knee over the entire gait cycle. Postive values indicates flexion. NOTE, the simulated knee is locked and can never be extended beyond 0 degress (straight leg). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Knee_Peak_extension.description: Peak extension of the knee over the entire gait cycle. Postive values indicates flexion. NOTE, the simulated knee is locked and can never be extended beyond 0 degress (straight leg). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Knee_ROM.description: Range of Motion (ROM): Anterior-posterior ROM of the knee joint over an entire gait cycle (heelstrike to heelstrike). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Hip_Heelstrike.description: Heelstrike: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the hip at heelstrike. Postive values indicate flexion and negative values indicate extension. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Hip_Mid_stance.description: Mid-stance: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the hip at mid-stance (when the ankle is directly beneath the hip joint centre). Postive values indicate flexion and negative values indicate extension. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Hip_Toeoff.description: Toeoff: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the hip at toeoff. Postive values indicate flexion and negative values indicate extension. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Hip_Mid_swing.description: Mid-swing: Anterior-posterior joint angle of the hip at mid-swing (when the ankle is directly beneath the hip joint centre). Postive values indicate flexion and negative values indicate extension. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Hip_Peak_flexion.description: Peak flexion of the hip over the entire gait cycle. Postive values indicates flexion and negative values indicates extension. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Hip_Peak_extension.description: Peak extension of the hip over the entire gait cycle. Postive values indicates flexion and negative values indicates extension. The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Hip_ROM.description: Range of Motion (ROM): Anterior-posterior ROM of the hip joint over an entire gait cycle (heelstrike to heelstrike). The left mean/std graph values were calculated on the left leg, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated on the right leg.

Pelvis_Peak_Pelvis_Obliquity.description: Peak Pelvis List (Obliquity): Peak medio-lateral list/obliquity of the pelvis accross one full stride (left and right strides). Positive values represent that the ipsilateral side is higher than the contralateral side, and negative values representing the ipsilateral side is lower than the contralateral side. Therefore, for the right side (grey dot), a positive value indicates that at one some point in the stride, the right side of the pelvis is higher than the left by that amount. See Angle_Graph of pelvis list angle over the entire stride for information across the whole stride. The left mean/std graph values were calculated during the left stride, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated during the right stride.

Pelvis_Average_Pelvis_Obliquity.description: Average Pelvis Obliquity: Average mediolateral list/obliquity of the pelvis accross one full stride of the right leg. Therefore, a positive value indicates that on average over one stride, the right side of the pelvis was higher than the left side, while a negtive value indicates the opposite. Because this is the average value over one stride, normal gait is expected to be very close to zero due to symetrical gait, while assymetry on one side of the body will result in a postive or negative number.

Trunk_Peak_Lateral_Trunk_Lean.description: Peak Lateral Trunk Lean: Peak medio-lateral trunk angle relative to vertical (gravity). When the value is positive, this indicates that the trunk is leaning towards the leg in contact with the ground, relative to a vertical line (gravity). Therefore, in the graph of the right side/stride, a postive value means that the trunk is leaning towards the right side, while a negative value indicates the trunk is leaning towards the left side. In the left side graph, it would be the opposite. The left mean/std graph values were calculated during the left stride, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated during the right stride.

Trunk_Peak_Forward_Trunk_Lean.description: Peak Forward Trunk Lean: Peak anterior-posterior trunk angle relative to vertical (gravity). When the value is positive, this indicates that the trunk is leaning forwards, relative to a vertical line (gravity). The left mean/std graph values were calculated during the left stride, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated during the right stride.

Trunk_Average_Forward_Trunk_Lean.description: Average Forward Trunk Lean: Average anterior-posterior trunk angle relative to vertical (gravity). When the value is positive, this indicates that on average, the trunk is leaning forwards accross the entire stride, relative to a vertical line (gravity). The left mean/std graph values were calculated during the left stride, while the right mean/std graph values were calculated during the right stride.

ankle.description: Anterior-posterior ankle angles over one stride, with positive values representing dorsiflexion and negative values representing plantar flexion. Joint angles for the ankle are time normalised to one full stride, so 0% on the x-axis repreesnts heel-strike, and 100% represents the following heel-strike for the same side/leg. In normal walking, toe-off will generally occur at 60% of the stride, thus stance can be viewed as between 0-60% and swing as between 60-100% on the x-axis

knee.description: Anterior-posterior knee angles over one stride, with positive values representing flexion and negative values representing extension. NOTE, the simulated knee is locked and can never be extended beyond 0 degress (straight leg). Joint angles for the knee are time normalised to one full stride, so 0% on the x-axis repreesnts heel-strike, and 100% represents the following heel-strike for the same side/leg. In normal walking, toe-off will generally occur at 60% of the stride, thus stance can generally be viewed as between 0-60% and swing as between 60-100% on the x-axis.

hip.description: Anterior-posterior hip angles over one stride, with positive values representing flexion and negative values representing extension. Joint angles for the hip are time normalised to one full stride, so 0% on the x-axis repreesnts heel-strike, and 100% represents the following heel-strike for the same side/leg. In normal walking, toe-off will generally occur at 60% of the stride, thus stance can be viewed as between 0-60% and swing as between 60-100% on the x-axis

pelvis.description: Medio-lateral list/obliquity for the pelvis angles over one stride, with positive values representing contralateral drop and negative values representing contralateral rise. Joint angles for the pelvis are time normalised to one full stride, so 0% on the x-axis repreesnts heel-strike, and 100% represents the following heel-strike for the same side/leg. In normal walking, toe-off will generally occur at 60% of the stride, thus stance can be viewed as between 0-60% and swing as between 60-100% on the x-axis
